chunks: PCB versus IC. The question: What is the difference between a PCB and IC?
An IC (integrated circuit) is a tiny piece of silicon where transistors and their wiring are built together at nanometer scale, then sealed in a package.
A PCB is the larger board that the packaged ICs, resistors, capacitors and connectors are soldered onto, with copper traces wiring them together.
The IC is where the active work happens: switching, amplifying and computing. The PCB mostly connects. ICs take months and a lot of money to make, and they cannot be modified.
PCBs take days and can be reworked.
Think of a city. The PCB is the street map: roads connect buildings, and you can add a bridge or close a road with a small effort.
The IC is a skyscraper with billions of tiny rooms and corridors inside, all built at once from a master plan. You cannot move a wall once the tower is built.
Inside the tower the corridors (wires) are very thin and resistive, while city streets are wide.
A transistor sits inside a die, the die in a package, packages on a PCB, PCBs in a product.
Each step multiplies the length scale by roughly 10 to 1000, and each step adds parasitics that the lower level did not have.
Die: the piece of silicon cut from a wafer that holds the integrated circuit. Package: the housing with pins or balls that lets a die be soldered to a board.
Photolithography: patterning with light, used at nanometer scale for ICs. Metal stack: the layers of on-chip wiring above the transistors.
Parasitics: unwanted resistance, inductance and capacitance.
Compare the wires. An on-chip copper wire 1 µm wide and 0. 2 µm thick has a resistance of about 85 ohms per millimeter. A PCB trace 0. 25 mm wide and 35 µm thick has only about 1.
7 times 10 to the -8 over (0. 25 times 10 to the -3 times 35 times 10 to the -6) equals 1. 9 milliohms per millimeter, about 40,000 times less.
But chip distances are around 100 times shorter and the loads are tiny, so chips are faster and use less power overall. That is the whole idea.
"An IC is a piece of silicon with transistors and nanometre-scale wiring fabricated together, put in a package.
A PCB is the board that ICs and other parts are soldered onto, with copper traces connecting them. So ICs are the active devices and a PCB is mostly interconnect and support.
IC features are nanometres to microns, PCB traces about a tenth of a millimetre.
ICs take months in a cleanroom with huge tooling cost and can't be modified, while PCBs take days and can be reworked."
